Annotate protein sequences with domains used for TF classification

Source: R/01_domain_annotation.R
annotate_domains.Rd

Protein sequences are scanned with HMMER for the domains used by the classification schemes of choice (see list_schemes()). Each domain annotation set has its own profile HMMs and filtering criteria:

  • PlantTFDB: PFAM and self-built profile HMMs, with the domain-specific score cutoffs defined by PlantTFDB (or an E-value threshold, for domains without cutoffs).

  • TAPscan: TAPscan v4 profile HMMs, with their gathering (GA) thresholds, as in the original TAPscan implementation.

  • CISBP: Pfam profile HMMs of the DNA-binding domains used by CIS-BP, with the thresholds used by CIS-BP (per-sequence E-value < 0.01 and per-domain conditional E-value < 0.01). As in CIS-BP, overlapping hits of different domains are resolved by keeping only the most significant hit (lowest independent E-value).

Usage

annotate_domains(seq = NULL, scheme = "all", evalue = 1e-05, threads = 1)

Arguments

seq

An AAStringSet object. The sequences in this object must represent only the translated sequences of primary (or longest) transcripts. To create such an object from a FASTA file, use Biostrings::readAAStringSet().

scheme

Character vector indicating the classification scheme(s) for which domains will be annotated. One or more of the schemes in list_schemes(), or 'all' to annotate domains for all schemes. Default: 'all'.

evalue

Numeric indicating the E-value threshold for hmmsearch to be used for PlantTFDB domains without pre-defined domain cutoffs. Default: 1e-05.

threads

Numeric indicating the number of threads to be used by hmmsearch. Default: 1.

Value

A list of data frames with domain annotation for each domain annotation set required by the chosen scheme(s) (PlantTFDB, TAPscan, and/or CISBP; see variable Annotation in list_schemes()). All data frames have one row per domain hit and the following variables:

Gene

Character, gene ID.

Domain

Character, domain ID or name.

qlen

Numeric, length of the profile HMM.

c_evalue

Numeric, conditional E-value of the domain hit.

hmm_from, hmm_to

Numeric, start and end coordinates of the alignment in the profile HMM.

Rows are kept in the same order as in the HMMER output, as this order is used by the TAPscan classification algorithm.

Examples

data(gsu)
seq <- gsu[1:5]
if(hmmer_is_installed()) {
    annotate_domains(seq)

    # Only domains used by CIS-BP's scheme
    annotate_domains(seq, scheme = "CISBP")
}
